title: Naturality with normalized scalar endpoints
statement: Let A and B be categories with integer shifts, L:A to B and R:B to A functors commuting with shifts, and ad:L adjoint to R a shift-compatible adjunction. Let X,Y,XR,YR be objects of A, Xprime,Yprime objects of B, e:L(X) isomorphic to Xprime, a:L(Y) to Yprime, ux:R(Xprime) isomorphic to XR and uy:R(Yprime) isomorphic to YR. Suppose the unit followed by R(e) and ux is q:X to XR, and the unit followed by R(a) and uy is r:Y to YR. For every integer n and f:X to Y[n], restriction of the scalar arrow e inverse, L(f), the L shift comparison and a[n], transported by ux and uy and precomposed with q, equals f followed by r[n].

source.place: clause (2), scalar extension and finite evaluation

proof.text: Substitute the source normalization and cancel ux with its inverse and R(e) with R(e inverse).
Use naturality of the adjunction unit on f. Commute the unit and the restriction comparison with the shift. The target normalization identifies the remaining shifted composite with r[n].

theorem normalizedScalarArrow_transpose
    {A B : Type*} [Category A] [Category B] [HasShift A ℤ] [HasShift B ℤ]
    (L : A ⥤ B) (R : B ⥤ A) [L.CommShift ℤ] [R.CommShift ℤ]
    (ad : L ⊣ R) [ad.CommShift ℤ]
    {X Y XR YR : A} {X' Y' : B}
    (e : L.obj X ≅ X') (a : L.obj Y ⟶ Y')
    (ux : R.obj X' ≅ XR) (uy : R.obj Y' ≅ YR)
    (q : X ⟶ XR) (r : Y ⟶ YR)
    (hx : ad.unit.app X ≫ R.map e.hom ≫ ux.hom = q)
    (hy : ad.unit.app Y ≫ R.map a ≫ uy.hom = r)
    (n : ℤ) (f : X ⟶ Y⟦n⟧) :
    q ≫ ux.inv ≫ R.map (e.inv ≫ L.map f ≫
        (L.commShiftIso n).hom.app Y ≫ a⟦n⟧') ≫
        (R.commShiftIso n).hom.app Y' ≫ uy.hom⟦n⟧' = f ≫ r⟦n⟧'
